subject: maths
title: Primary 4 Multiplication
seo_title: P4 Multiplication Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Multiplication algorithm up to 4 digits by 1 digit and up to 3 digits by 2 digits
meta_desc: Free P4 multiplication worksheets: 4-digit × 1-digit, 2-digit × 2-digit and 3-digit × 2-digit, renaming, estimates and bar models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply from the ones, add the renamed digit after multiplying, and start the second row with 0.
body_html:
4-digit × 1-digit: multiply, then rename

Start with the ones. Multiply one digit at a time. If a product is 10 or more, write the ones digit and rename the tens into the next column. Multiply first, then add the renamed digit.

2-digit × 2-digit: the area model

Split both numbers into tens and ones. Multiply each part, then add all four parts.

The algorithm: one row for each digit

The first row multiplies by the ones digit. The second row multiplies by the tens digit, so it starts with 0 in the ones place (green). Then add the two rows.

3-digit × 2-digit

It works the same way. The rows are just longer.

Estimate to check

Is 243 × 36 = 8748 reasonable?

Round 243 to the nearest hundred and 36 to the nearest ten: 200 × 40 = 8000. 8748 is close to 8000, so it makes sense. 2187 (no 0 in the second row) is far off.

Answer: Yes

Word problems: draw a model

“4 times as many” means 4 equal units. Find 1 unit, then multiply.

How many more?

Siti has 325 stickers. Wei Ming has 4 times as many. How many more stickers does Wei Ming have?

Wei Ming has 4 units and Siti has 1 unit, so the difference is 3 units: 3 × 325 = 975.

Answer: 975 stickers

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the 0 in the second row (38 × 24 = 152 + 76 = 228)The second row is × 20, so write 0 first: 760
Not adding the renamed digit (2367 × 4 = 8248)Write it small above the next column and add it: 6 × 4 + 2 = 26
Adding before multiplying ((6 + 2) × 4 = 32)Multiply first, then add: 6 × 4 + 2 = 26
Only two parts in the area model (23 × 14 = 200 + 12)There are four parts: 200 + 30 + 80 + 12 = 322

faq.q: What multiplication is taught in P4 maths?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students multiply up to a 4-digit number by a 1-digit number and up to a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number, such as 2367 × 4 and 243 × 36. They also estimate to check their answers and solve word problems.

faq.q: How do I explain 2-digit by 2-digit multiplication to my child?
faq.a: Start with the area model: split both numbers into tens and ones and add the four parts, so 23 × 14 = 200 + 30 + 80 + 12 = 322. Then show the algorithm, where each row is one row of the area model.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in P4 multiplication?
faq.a: Forgetting the 0 at the start of the second row. In 38 × 24 the 2 means 2 tens, so the row is 38 × 20 = 760, not 76. Not adding the renamed digit is the next most common mistake.

faq.q: Is multiplication by 2-digit numbers in the MOE Primary 4 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics syllabus has the multiplication algorithm up to 4 digits by 1 digit and up to 3 digits by 2 digits in Primary 4. These skills are used in every later topic and in the PSLE.

items.q: A theatre sells 1985 tickets for each show. About how many tickets does it sell for 4 shows?
items.e: Round 1985 to the nearest thousand: 2000. 2000 × 4 = 8000. (Rounding 1985 down to 1000 gives 4000, far too small.) The exact answer is 1985 × 4 = 7940.

items.q: Kavya reads 28 pages of a storybook each day. About how many pages does she read in 31 days?
items.e: Round 28 to 30 and 31 to 30. 30 × 30 = 900. (Using 20 × 30 = 600 rounds 28 the wrong way.) The exact answer is 28 × 31 = 868.

items.q: Use an estimate. Which of these is the value of 706 × 49?
items.e: Estimate: 706 × 49 is about 700 × 50 = 35 000. Only 34 594 is close to 35 000. (9178 forgot the 0 in the second row; 345 940 has one 0 too many; 755 comes from adding.)

items.q: Ahmad worked out 72 × 39 = 2808. Estimate to check. Is his answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 72 × 39 is about 70 × 40 = 2800. 2808 is close to 2800, so the answer is reasonable.

items.q: A school orders 19 boxes of exercise books at $42 a box. About how much is the total cost?
items.e: Round 19 to 20 and $42 to $40. 20 × $40 = $800. The exact cost is 19 × $42 = $798, very close. (Rounding $42 up to $50 gives $1000, which is too far off.)

items.q: Use an estimate. Which of these is the value of 84 × 33?
items.e: Estimate: 84 × 33 is about 80 × 30 = 2400. Only 2772 is close to 2400. (504 forgot the 0 in the second row; 27 720 has one 0 too many; 117 comes from adding.)

items.q: Ali worked out 563 × 28 = 5630. Estimate to check. Is his answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 563 × 28 is about 600 × 30 = 18 000. 5630 is far from 18 000, so it cannot be right. Ali forgot the 0 in the second row. The correct answer is 15 764.

items.q: Use an estimate. Which of these is the value of 392 × 61?
items.e: Estimate: 392 × 61 is about 400 × 60 = 24 000. Only 23 912 is close to 24 000. (2744 forgot the 0 in the second row; 239 120 has one 0 too many; 453 comes from adding.)

items.q: Round 487 to the nearest hundred and 32 to the nearest ten to estimate 487 × 32.
items.e: 487 rounds up to 500 and 32 rounds down to 30. 500 × 30 = 15 000. The exact answer is 15 584, close to the estimate.

items.q: The school canteen sells 312 plates of fried rice each week. About how many plates does it sell in 8 weeks?
items.e: Round 312 to the nearest hundred: 300. 300 × 8 = 2400. Do not round 8 to 10: that gives 3000, which is too far off. The exact answer is 312 × 8 = 2496.

items.q: Use an estimate. Which of these is the value of 59 × 47?
items.e: Estimate: 59 × 47 is about 60 × 50 = 3000. Only 2773 is close to 3000. (649 forgot the 0 in the second row; 27 730 has one 0 too many; 106 comes from adding.)

items.q: Round 624 to the nearest hundred and 58 to the nearest ten to estimate 624 × 58.
items.e: 624 rounds down to 600 and 58 rounds up to 60. 600 × 60 = 36 000. The exact answer is 36 192, close to the estimate.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate 67 × 48.
items.e: 67 rounds up to 70 and 48 rounds up to 50. 70 × 50 = 3500. The exact answer is 3216, close to the estimate.

items.q: Round 3746 to the nearest thousand to estimate 3746 × 4.
items.e: 3746 has 7 hundreds, so it rounds up to 4000. 4000 × 4 = 16 000. The exact answer is 14 984.

items.q: A stadium has 48 rows with 215 seats in each row. About how many seats are there?
items.e: Round 215 to 200 and 48 to 50. 200 × 50 = 10 000. (Rounding 48 down to 40 gives 8000.) The exact answer is 215 × 48 = 10 320.

items.q: Mei Ling worked out 46 × 27 = 414. Estimate to check. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 46 × 27 is about 50 × 30 = 1500. 414 is far from 1500, so it cannot be right. Mei Ling forgot the 0 in the second row. The correct answer is 1242.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate 83 × 26.
items.e: 83 rounds down to 80 and 26 rounds up to 30. 80 × 30 = 2400. The exact answer is 2158, close to the estimate.

items.q: Raju worked out 318 × 42 = 13 356. Estimate to check. Is his answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 318 × 42 is about 300 × 40 = 12 000. 13 356 is close to 12 000, so the answer is reasonable.

items.q: Siti worked out 58 × 34 = 406. Estimate to check. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 58 × 34 is about 60 × 30 = 1800. 406 is far from 1800, so it cannot be right. Siti forgot the 0 in the second row. The correct answer is 1972.

items.q: Round 6281 to the nearest thousand to estimate 6281 × 3.
items.e: 6281 has 2 hundreds, so it rounds down to 6000. 6000 × 3 = 18 000. The exact answer is 18 843.

items.q: The school hall has 28 rows of seats. There are 36 seats in each row. How many seats are there in the hall?
items.e: 28 rows × 36 seats, so multiply 36 × 28. Row 1: 36 × 8 = 288. Row 2: 36 × 20 = 720 (write 0 in the ones place, then 36 × 2 = 72). Add: 288 + 720 = 1008.

items.q: A box holds 12 eggs. A supermarket sells 365 boxes of eggs in a week. How many eggs does it sell?
items.e: 365 boxes × 12 eggs, so multiply 365 × 12. Row 1: 365 × 2 = 730. Row 2: 365 × 10 = 3650 (write 0 in the ones place, then 365 × 1 = 365). Add: 730 + 3650 = 4380.

items.q: A carton holds 18 eggs. A shop has 245 cartons of eggs. How many eggs does the shop have?
items.e: 245 cartons × 18 eggs, so multiply 245 × 18. Row 1: 245 × 8 = 1960. Row 2: 245 × 10 = 2450 (write 0 in the ones place, then 245 × 1 = 245). Add: 1960 + 2450 = 4410.

items.q: A stadium has 46 rows with 128 seats in each row. How many seats are there?
items.e: 46 rows × 128 seats, so multiply 128 × 46. Row 1: 128 × 6 = 768. Row 2: 128 × 40 = 5120 (write 0 in the ones place, then 128 × 4 = 512). Add: 768 + 5120 = 5888.

items.q: A bakery bakes 1475 kaya buns each day. How many kaya buns does it bake in 6 days?
items.e: 6 days × 1475 buns, so multiply 1475 × 6. 5 × 6 = 30, write 0, rename 3; 7 × 6 + 3 = 45, write 5, rename 4; 4 × 6 + 4 = 28, write 8, rename 2; 1 × 6 + 2 = 8, write 8. Answer: 8850 kaya buns.

items.q: A train carries 1286 passengers on each trip. How many passengers does it carry on 7 trips?
items.e: 7 trips × 1286 passengers, so multiply 1286 × 7. 6 × 7 = 42, write 2, rename 4; 8 × 7 + 4 = 60, write 0, rename 6; 2 × 7 + 6 = 20, write 0, rename 2; 1 × 7 + 2 = 9, write 9. Answer: 9002 passengers.

items.q: A school buys 9 laptops at $1245 each. How much does the school pay?
items.e: 9 laptops × $1245, so multiply 1245 × 9. 5 × 9 = 45, write 5, rename 4; 4 × 9 + 4 = 40, write 0, rename 4; 2 × 9 + 4 = 22, write 2, rename 2; 1 × 9 + 2 = 11, write 11. Answer: $11 205.

items.q: For Chinese New Year, a shop packs mandarin oranges in boxes of 24. It packs 156 boxes. How many mandarin oranges are there?
items.e: 156 boxes × 24 oranges, so multiply 156 × 24. Row 1: 156 × 4 = 624. Row 2: 156 × 20 = 3120 (write 0 in the ones place, then 156 × 2 = 312). Add: 624 + 3120 = 3744.

items.q: A bus can take 42 students. For Sports Day, the school books 17 buses. How many students can the buses take?
items.e: 17 buses × 42 students, so multiply 42 × 17. Row 1: 42 × 7 = 294. Row 2: 42 × 10 = 420 (write 0 in the ones place, then 42 × 1 = 42). Add: 294 + 420 = 714.

items.q: A fruit seller has 27 baskets of rambutans. There are 48 rambutans in each basket. How many rambutans are there?
items.e: 27 baskets × 48 rambutans, so multiply 48 × 27. Row 1: 48 × 7 = 336. Row 2: 48 × 20 = 960 (write 0 in the ones place, then 48 × 2 = 96). Add: 336 + 960 = 1296.

items.q: Xin Yi's school has 213 students in Primary 4. Each student gets 14 worksheets for the holidays. How many worksheets must the school print?
items.e: 213 students × 14 worksheets, so multiply 213 × 14. Row 1: 213 × 4 = 852. Row 2: 213 × 10 = 2130 (write 0 in the ones place, then 213 × 1 = 213). Add: 852 + 2130 = 2982.

items.q: The school library has 135 shelves. Each shelf holds 64 books. How many books can the shelves hold?
items.e: 135 shelves × 64 books, so multiply 135 × 64. Row 1: 135 × 4 = 540. Row 2: 135 × 60 = 8100 (write 0 in the ones place, then 135 × 6 = 810). Add: 540 + 8100 = 8640.

items.q: Ali saved $1356. His sister Nurul saved 4 times as much as Ali. How much did Nurul save?
Kumar has 236 stamps. Raju has 5 times as many stamps as Kumar. How many more stamps does Raju have than Kumar?
items.e: Raju has 5 units and Kumar has 1 unit, so Raju has 4 units more. 1 unit = 236. 4 units = 4 × 236 = 944. (5 × 236 = 1180 is how many stamps Raju has.)

items.q: There were 1275 visitors at a museum on Monday. There were 3 times as many visitors on Saturday. How many visitors were there on the two days altogether?
items.e: Monday is 1 unit and Saturday is 3 units, so the two days are 4 units. 1 unit = 1275. 4 units = 4 × 1275 = 5100. (3825 is Saturday only.)

items.q: Each of the 6 Primary 4 classes collected 1248 cans for recycling. How many cans did they collect altogether?
items.e: 6 units, 1 unit = 1248. 6 × 1248: 8 × 6 = 48, write 8, rename 4; 4 × 6 + 4 = 28, write 8, rename 2; 2 × 6 + 2 = 14, write 4, rename 1; 1 × 6 + 1 = 7. Answer: 7488 cans.

items.q: Mdm Wong bought 7 boxes of exercise books with 145 books in each box. She gave out 238 books. How many books did she have left?
For the school concert, the hall is set up with 24 rows of 35 chairs. 768 parents come. How many chairs are empty?
items.e: Step 1: chairs: 35 × 24 (first row: 35 × 4 = 140; second row: 35 × 20 = 700; 140 + 700 = 840). Step 2: empty chairs: 840 − 768 = 72.

items.q: Mr Rahman buys 15 tickets for a school show at $36 each. He pays with $600. How much change does he get?
A farm packs 125 boxes of 12 eggs and 84 trays of 30 eggs. How many eggs does it pack altogether?
items.e: Boxes: 125 × 12 = 1500 eggs. Trays: 84 × 30 = 2520 eggs. Altogether: 1500 + 2520 = 4020 eggs. (5 hundreds + 5 hundreds = 10 hundreds: rename 1 thousand.)
